passage: On a rainy afternoon in Istanbul, Elif sat the doll on a cushion and said to Amara, "You are sick. I listen to your chest. Then I give medicine. Okay?" Amara nodded. Elif turned to the doll and practised the first line, "Open your mouth, please," in a serious voice, tapping a toy stethoscope on the doll's tummy. Then Elif looked back at Amara. "Now you."

qa.q: What does Elif say will come after listening to the chest?
What was Elif feeling while talking through the game?
qa.a: Elif was serious and excited, wanting the game to go well and feeling in charge of it.

qa.q: What alternative could Elif use if Amara wants a different game, and why?
qa.a: Elif could ask Amara what part Amara wants to play, because a plan works better when both players agree on it.

qa.q: How does Amara see Elif's plan for the doctor game?
qa.a: Amara nods at the plan and probably feels included and curious, having been told the roles and steps in advance.

grounding: A child talks through a doctor game ahead of time, saying what the sick person and doctor will do, and acts out the first lines with a doll.

passage: In the kindergarten corner, Amandeep sat Mridul on a cushion. "Okay, you're sick. Your tummy hurts. I'll listen to your heart, then I'll give you medicine." She held a pretend stethoscope to her doll first. "Breathe in. Good. Now you say ow." "Ow," said the doll, in her voice. "Now you, Mridul." Mridul giggled and said, "Ow!"

qa.a: She sat Mridul on a cushion.

qa.q: What was Amandeep thinking as she tried it on the doll first?
qa.a: She felt eager and serious, practising the lines so the real game would go right.

qa.q: What else could Amandeep do to plan the game?
qa.a: She could ask Mridul which role to play, so the plan fits both of them.

qa.q: How does the game look to Mridul?
qa.a: Mridul finds it funny and fun, giggling and playing along.

grounding: A child rehearses a doctor game ahead of time, saying the steps and acting out the first lines with a doll.

passage: I'm Kiran, and Vishal is my classmate's little brother. At their house I watched him set up a pretend clinic. He whispered to a teddy, "You're sick. I listen to your heart. Then medicine." He pressed a bottle cap to its chest and said, "Breathe!" Then he whispered it all again. I think he was practising before his sister came, but maybe he just liked talking to the teddy.

qa.q: What did Vishal press to the teddy's chest?
qa.a: He pressed a bottle cap to its chest.

qa.q: What was Kiran thinking as Vishal whispered it all again?
qa.a: Kiran was curious and unsure, wondering if Vishal was practising or just enjoying talking to the teddy.

qa.q: What else could help Vishal plan the game?
qa.a: He could ask his sister what she wants to be, so the game fits them both.

qa.q: How might Vishal feel when his sister arrives?
qa.a: He would probably feel ready and excited, because he already practised the lines.

grounding: An observer watches a child rehearse a doctor game out loud with a teddy before playing it.
